This location would also allow for towed tests via the CEC supporting mechanism or the A-frame. The mean speed at this location is 1.5 m/s, and the maximum speed is 3 m/s, which falls under the design speed of 4 m/s specified in the SOPO. Regarding waves, for a 5-year return, a significant wave height of 6 m was observed, which presents the biggest wave conditions of all evaluated locations (discussed later in this section). Wind speeds at this location average 5 m/s, while the maximum wind recorded in 2021 was 21.5 m/s. However, from a cumulative probability distribution analysis, a maximum design wind speed of 18 m/s was chosen. 3.2.2 Tidal locations Tidal currents are caused by the movement of water associated with the rise and fall of the sea surface caused by the gravitational forces exerted on the Earth (mainly by the moon). In the U.S., tidal currents can be found in various states such as Alaska, Maine, Massachusetts, Washington, New York, California, Florida, and North Carolina. Velocities average between 0.55 and 2.22 m/s, with higher maximum velocities reached than ocean currents. These peaks can be as high as 5.2 m/s. Final Technical Report 16/57 Due to this broad range of possible conditions, efforts to characterize tidal sites were focused on the most optimal locations with the highest flow speeds: • Cook Inlet, AK • Admiralty Inlet, WA • Western Passage, ME • Piscataqua River, ME/NH For each of these locations, efforts were made to identify potential locations that would allow the use of the jack-up system and the internal mooring system when possible. Cook Inlet The optimal area of Cook Inlet is around Kalgin Island and The Forelands. Potential test areas near these locations could use either of the mooring systems mentioned above. Several buoys have been analyzed in this area; average speeds are around 2-2.5 m/s, while maximum speeds can reach 5.2 m/s. However, if figures showing cumulative probability distribution are considered, the design speed of 4 m/s covers most of the speeds found at this location. Waves are attenuated in the estuary, and the maximum significant wave height only reaches 1 m. Wind speeds average at 3.9 m/s, while maximum wind speed for 2021 was 16.6 m/s. Admiralty Inlet Admiralty Inlet is the busiest tidal location in terms of maritime traffic, which can pose a logistics challenge. One of the proposed locations is off Point Wilson, through which a navigable channel exists, and the MTV would have to be moored out of it. Regardless, there is the possibility of using the jack- up legs or the internal mooring system at this location, with the corresponding further bathymetry analysis. The other proposed location was chosen with PNNL’s support and is around the San Juan Islands.
